en.title: The Imitation Game: Please Stay Strange
en.html:
During the Second World War, the Allies struggle to crack Germany’s secret Enigma system. The government recruits civilian mathematicians and logicians for a secret codebreaking operation.

Turing, played by Benedict Cumberbatch, is one of them.

At the start, he faces rejection from his superiors and fellow team members, led by Hugh, played by Matthew Goode. Fortunately, intelligence chief Menzies, played by Mark Strong, helps him secure a project to build a codebreaking machine. Turing takes charge, recruits Joan, played by Keira Knightley, and begins the difficult work.

Joan soon becomes attracted to Turing. With her help, the team becomes more united than ever and successfully breaks the German code two years later. Turing is briefly engaged to Joan, but he is hiding a secret for which he will suffer inhuman treatment…

War hero or criminal?

Turing asks this question while being questioned by a police officer during the proceedings against him.

Although they have cracked Enigma, they cannot let Germany know. Turing therefore chooses to allow some attacks they already know about to happen—in other words, to let some people die.

When Christopher first begins to work, they identify the location of a German attack, and a colleague’s brother is aboard the targeted ship. This resembles the trolley problem: on one side is breaking the entire system and ending the war sooner; on the other, saving hundreds of living people.

However difficult the choice, Turing firmly decides to keep the secret, concealing the fact that Enigma has been broken.

Perhaps war’s cruelty lies not only in lives being lost, but also in not knowing when those losses will end.

We are not Turing and do not face his dilemma. Yet, judging by the outcome, his decision brought the war’s end forward by at least two years and saved more than fourteen million lives.

What is the difference between a person and a machine?

In the final twenty minutes of The Imitation Game, Turing faces the detective in an interrogation room and voices the film’s central question: what distinguishes people from machines? The most fundamental difference is that people think differently from one another, whereas machines do not. You love strawberries; I hate skating. You enjoy reading; I am allergic to pollen…

In the film, Turing argues that we cannot conclude that machines do not think simply because they think differently from humans.

Humans possess intelligence, and intelligence also brings arrogance.

Image source: Unsplash.

Sometimes it is the people no one imagines anything of who do the things no one can imagine

People others have little faith in are often people they do not understand.

We tend to accept views we agree with. Likewise, we tend to approach people we can understand.

Independent-minded. Strange. Unordinary.

If we fear being scorched by even a glance, how can we approach them, let alone recognise their worth?

“Let us stop mentioning Turing. His death makes us feel that all of us wronged him. Geniuses always approach this world occupied by mediocrities innocently, openly and without defences, offering it all their passion. The world often responds by tipping a basin of dirty water over their heads.”
—Mu Xin

Image source: Unsplash.

Loneliness, arrogance and prejudice

“We love each other in our own way. We can live the life we want together. You cannot be a perfect husband, and I do not want to be a perfect wife. I will not spend all day cooking lamb chops and waiting for you to come home from the office… We enjoy each other’s company and each other’s minds, because I care about you. We know one another better than anyone.”

Joan says this to Turing.

As a mathematically gifted woman who does not want to be confined to domestic chores, she too is lonely and misunderstood, wounded by men’s arrogance and prejudice.

There is so much prejudice in the world, and therefore so many lonely souls.

We discriminate against people of different races, different faiths and different sexual orientations. We discriminate against anyone whose ideas differ from ours, even people whose only difference is where they were born.

If technological progress could be disregarded, this world would have changed nothing in thousands upon thousands of years.

Prejudice is an immense gulf in the human heart. Its reason is simple: we are all so similarly small.

Image source: Unsplash.

zh.title: 推影｜《模仿游戏》：请保持怪异
zh.html:
二战期间，盟军苦于德国的秘密系统“英格玛”无法破译，政府召集了一批民间数学家、逻辑学家进行秘密破解工作。

图灵（本尼迪克特·康伯巴奇 Benedict Cumberbatch 饰）就是其中之一。

计划刚开始图灵遭到了以休（马修·古迪 Matthew Goode）为首的组员和领导的排斥，幸好军情处部长孟席斯（马克·斯特朗 Mark Strong 饰）帮助他立项研究破译密码的机器，而图灵则变成了负责人，招收了新的成员琼（凯拉·奈特莉 Keira Knightley）开始了艰难的工作。

琼很快就迷上了图灵，由于她的帮助所有组员空前的团结，并于两年后成功破解德军的密码。图灵一度与琼订婚，但实际上他隐瞒了一个秘密，因为这个秘密他也遭受了非人的待遇……

战争英雄还是罪犯？

在审判时被警官询问的时候，图灵问了这么一个问题。

尽管破解了德军的“英格玛”，但不能让德军知道，于是，图灵选择让一些已经知道的行动发生，也就是选择了让一些人死亡。

尤其是Christopher刚刚起作用时，他们破获了德军的一次袭击地点，并且图灵同事的哥哥也在这艘舰上，这实在有点“电车困境”的两难，一方面是破获整个揭秘系统，提早结束战争，一方面是拯救上百条鲜活的生命。

尽管再难以抉择，图灵还是坚定地选择了保守秘密，掩饰他们已经破解“英格玛”的真相。

战争的残酷或许不仅仅是生命的逝去，还有不知道这种逝去何时才能终止。

我们不是图灵，没有这种抉择的困境，但至少从结果来看，他的决定至少将战争结束的时间提早了两年，拯救了超过一千四百万生命。

人和机器的区别是什么？

在《模仿游戏》的最后二十分钟，在审讯室里，面对着探长的图灵说出了本剧的题眼：人和机器的区别是什么？二者最本质的区别是，人是有不同想法的，机器则不是。你爱草莓，我讨厌滑冰，你喜欢看书，我对花粉过敏……

影片中，图灵认为我们不能因为机器与人类思考的方式不同而认为它们不在思考。

人类有灵智，智慧同时带来了傲慢。

图片来源：Unsplash

有时候正是无人看好之人，成就了无人能及的成就

不被看好的人，往往是不被理解的人。

人们倾向于接受自己认同的观点，同样，人们也倾向于接近自己可理解的人。

特立独行、怪异、不普通。

连看一眼都怕被灼伤，谈何接近，谈何认可。

“别再提图灵了吧，他的死，使我们感到大家都是对不起他的。天才总天真、坦荡、毫不设防地迎向这个庸人占领的世界，一腔热诚付与世界。世界待他们，往往却是一盆脏水兜头浇下。”
——木心

图片来源：Unsplash

孤独、傲慢、偏见

“我们用自己的方式爱着对方，我们能一起过我们想要的生活，你成不了完美丈夫，我也不想做什么完美的妻子，我不会整天给你做羊排，等你从办公室下班回家…我们享受互相的陪伴，我们享受互相的思想，因为我在乎你。我们彼此相知，胜过任何人”

琼对图灵说。

作为有数学天赋的，不想被困于家庭琐事的女性，她的也是孤独的，不被理解的，被男人的傲慢和偏见中伤的。

世界上实在有太多偏见，于是有太多孤独的心灵。

我们歧视不同种族的人，我们歧视不同信仰的人，我们歧视不同性向的人，我们歧视任何观念与我们不合的人，我们甚歧视仅仅是出生地不同的人。

如果技术进步可以忽略不计，这个世界千万年来没任何改变。

偏见是人类心灵的巨大鸿沟，原因再简单不过，仅仅是我们都渺小的相似。

图片来源：Unsplash
